title: Anthropic hits three-hour multi-model Claude outage as Mythos, Fable, and Opus all fail
subtitle: An incident starting at 05:06 UTC on August 24 hit Claude Mythos 5, Fable 5, Opus 5, and Opus 4.8 across claude.ai, the API, Claude Code, and Cowork — resolved by 08:30 UTC with no root cause disclosed.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic's Claude platform experienced a broad multi-model outage on August 24, first flagged on the company's status page at 05:06 UTC. Elevated errors hit Claude Mythos 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, and Claude Opus 4.8 simultaneously across claude.ai, the api.anthropic.com developer endpoint, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. Anthropic identified a root cause internally at 05:27 UTC — roughly 21 minutes after the initial alert — but remediation stretched past 06:42 UTC before service was declared fully restored around 08:30 UTC. Total impact was roughly three hours. Anthropic has not publicly disclosed what the underlying fault was.

The pattern is what makes this notable. Individual model routes fail all the time — that's normal ops. Losing Mythos, Fable, Opus 5, and Opus 4.8 at once, across every product surface, points at something below the model-serving layer: a shared inference gateway, a routing plane, or an auth or rate-limiting component that fronts every request. That's the class of failure that takes API customers offline whether they've pinned a specific model or not, and it undercuts the standard multi-model failover pattern developers are told to build. Claude Code users on paid plans lost the tool for a full working morning in Europe.

This is Anthropic's second high-visibility reliability incident in six weeks. The July 10 event — the Claude Code usage-limit reset that spilled into hours-long API errors for Cowork users — hit a different subsystem but the same customer perception: the paid tier is where reliability is supposed to live, and it isn't holding. Anthropic reported $10.9 billion in Q2 revenue and its first operating profit in the same quarter, so the pressure is now to keep enterprise SLAs while the fleet triples. Not disclosing a root cause after a three-hour cross-product outage will not help the enterprise conversation.

A note for learners: if you build on a single model provider, an outage like this is your outage too. The standard mitigation is genuine multi-provider failover — the app degrades to a second-choice model on a different provider (Fable → GPT-5.6 Luna, Claude Code → Codex, and so on) when the primary returns errors above a threshold. That takes real engineering: consistent tool-call schemas, prompt portability, and a routing layer you own. Cheap 'we'll add a fallback later' plans do not survive a three-hour incident. Design as if the primary provider will be down for four hours next month, because sometimes it will be.
